why: The two N/A branches of the rule, one per folder. The heuristic only accuses hex that ALREADY EXISTS as a token in the CSS, because the naive version of it gave 100% false positives when measured — loose hex has far too much legitimate context, three.js material and overlay veil. `pass/` has no .css at all and `fail/` has a .css written only with named colors: in both the token table comes out empty, and with no table the comparison does not exist. Swapping either of the two `na` for `null` makes the heuristic claim "no duplicated color" in a repository where it looked at no color at all. `na` stays as it is: it is the state value prove.mjs matches on (prove.mjs:198-200), not prose.
